title: Data residency discovery - Oceanside Financial

Priya to schedule technical deep-dive and scoping session for dedicated pool benchmarking
Customer to provide logging/retention requirements and key stakeholders for legal review
Agree on timeline for pilot (target: pilot start week of 2026-03-30)
action_items: Alex Monroe: Send SOC2 report, HIPAA summary, and Redwood DPA template (due: 2026-03-13)
Priya Kapoor: Schedule technical deep-dive and share benchmarking runbook (due: 2026-03-16)
Sam Patel: Share sample query workload and list of PII/PHI types to test obfuscation (due: 2026-03-15)

summary: Intro discovery with Oceanside Financial to map compliance constraints for possible Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Customer requires EU and US data residency options, HIPAA controls for some workflows, strict logging retention rules and RBAC/SSO integration. Next steps: send SOC2/HIPAA docs, schedule technical deep-dive, and scope pilot benchmarks.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood. We have Priya from our infra team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Karen Liu: Good, thanks. Karen here, CISO at Oceanside. Sorry if I'm a bit early, juggling another thing.
[00:12] Miguel Torres: Miguel, head of compliance. Hi all.
[00:14] Sam Patel: Sam, platform engineer.
[00:16] Alex Monroe: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll do a quick intro, understand your requirements on data residency and compliance, confirm technical constraints, and outline next steps. Priya will jump in on the more technical questions. Sound good?
[00:26] Karen Liu: Yep.
[00:28] Priya Kapoor: Yep, thanks Alex.
[00:30] [00:30] Alex Monroe: To kick off, can you give us a little bit of context around the projects you want to use inference for and where the data is coming from?
[00:38] Miguel Torres: Sure. We're building a customer support summarization and internal document search tool. A subset of workflows will include PII and some PHI — we do very limited health data for small merchant customers — so HIPAA is in the mix. Most documents are stored in S3 in AWS US-EAST and a secondary copy in our EU region for GDPR purposes. We have strict SLAs for latency on some features, but for the PII/PHI paths we need stronger controls.
[01:05] Alex Monroe: Got it. So mix of PII/PHI, multi-region copies and latency-sensitive routes. Are you prototyping on our hosted API or considering Dedicated/Private from the start?
[01:16] Sam Patel: We're evaluating. We like the idea of Hosted for speed to market but Miguel and Karen are concerned about residency and log retention. Dedicated seems interesting if we can guarantee data doesn't leave our reserved pool. Private might be needed for the HIPAA flows or regulated customers.
[01:31] Priya Kapoor: That aligns with what we typically see. Redwood Hosted is our fastest to get started, but by default hosted is multi-tenant and logs are stored per our retention policies; we can limit logging of payloads and have controls, but Dedicated gives isolated compute and options to disable persistent request logs. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the most control — e.g., no egress to Redwood-managed network and customer-managed KMS.
[01:55] Karen Liu: For HIPAA we need a signed BA, and we need to know where PHI is stored and how it's logged. Do you have a HIPAA BAA?
[02:04] Alex Monroe: Yes, we have a HIPAA addendum. We'll share our BAA and the HIPAA controls matrix. For Hosted customers we support HIPAA under a BA but there are constraints: e.g., some customers prefer Dedicated or Private for PHI.
[02:16] Miguel Torres: And GDPR — we need EU data residency for EU customers. Can you ensure model inference and logs stay in EU region only?
[02:24] Priya Kapoor: We can. For Dedicated we offer region pinning so your Dedicated pool runs in eu-west-1 only. For Hosted, we route regionally but hosted can still have control plane components in our primary region; we can provide data residency guarantees in Dedicated/Private. Private VPC gets you full control.
[02:42] Sam Patel: On encryption, we use KMS in our account for keys. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[02:49] Priya Kapoor: Yes, Private deployments support customer-managed KMS or HSM integrations. For Dedicated we support bring-your-own-KMS via a customer-managed key in cloud provider — we'll describe the setup in the runbook. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we can provide envelope encryption and key separation for some customers.
[03:06] Alex Monroe: Quick question on logs: what exactly is logged? Request/response bodies, prompts, top-k completions etc.
[03:13] Priya Kapoor: Default hosted logs request metadata and truncated prompts for debugging, but we can disable full request/response logging. With Dedicated/Private you can disable logging of request bodies entirely and only keep structured metrics and traces. Note: disabling logs removes some observability features we'll need to compensate for.
[03:30] Karen Liu: We also need retention policies — we cannot keep any prompts containing financial info longer than 30 days, and some regulatory artifacts need 7 years for audit records but those must be redacted.
[03:41] Miguel Torres: Right, so two needs: short retention for sensitive PII/PHI and long retention for certain audit logs that must be anonymized. Can you do both?
[03:49] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can support tiered retention. On Dedicated/Private we can configure short TTLs on request payload storage, and have separate immutable audit trails that store structured events with PII redacted or hashed. We'll need to align on what fields must be redacted.
[04:07] Alex Monroe: Is there a preference on token-level auditing vs event-level?
[04:10] Karen Liu: Event-level with obfuscation is preferred. We can't have raw utterances stored unless they are strictly necessary.
[04:16] Priya Kapoor: Understood. We'll propose an architecture where raw requests are ephemeral, only normalized events are stored to your audit log with deterministic hashing for identifiers you want reversible, and irreversible hashing for user content. We can also work with your legal team on exact hashing schemes.
[04:34] Sam Patel: On the technical deep-dive, we want to test latency. If we pin a dedicated pool in eu-west-1, what latency numbers can we expect for our 512-token regressions?
[04:44] Priya Kapoor: It depends on model and instance type. Roughly, for a 7B open model on a dedicated 8xA100 pool you'd see P95 around 120-200ms per token under steady-state with current kernels — but we should run a benchmark on your exact workload. We'll include batching and KV cache notes in the runbook.
[05:02] Miguel Torres: About model selection: do you host open models or only your curated ones? We have concerns about model provenance and licensing.
[05:10] Alex Monroe: We host a model catalog — curated open models and Redwood-verified variants. For sensitive workflows you can choose a vetted open model or a private model in Private deployment. We also support pinning model versions for reproducibility.
[05:24] Karen Liu: Can you speak to SOC2 and third-party audits?
[05:27] Alex Monroe: Yes, we will share our SOC2 Type II report. We undergo annual audits and have ISO 27001 certifications in progress. For enterprise deployments we can provide audit artifacts and support AICPA-style requests.
[05:40] Miguel Torres: Regarding legal/procurement, we'll need a DPA and to confirm Redwood's subprocessors list.
[05:45] Alex Monroe: We'll include the DPA template and a current subprocessors list in the packet we send.
[05:49] [06:00] Karen Liu: A couple of edge concerns: e-discovery — if regulators request logs, what's the process?
[06:07] Priya Kapoor: For Hosted we handle lawful disclosure requests per our legal process; for Dedicated/Private, you can manage disclosure and we can assist with exports. We'll need to add contractual commitments about notification windows.
[06:20] Sam Patel: On networking: for Private, do you support an on-prem option or only VPC peering?
[06:26] Priya Kapoor: Both. We have a VPC-hosted private control plane option and a deployable on-prem package for customers who need full air-gapped setups. On-prem is more involved but doable.
[06:36] Miguel Torres: Cost — what's the uplift for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private?
[06:41] Alex Monroe: Quick summary: Hosted is usage-based and typically lowest up-front cost. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) — higher base but predictable unit economics and isolation. Private has platform licensing and support fees on top. We'll send a pricing snapshot for a 6-month pilot.
[06:58] Karen Liu: For HIPAA, I want to confirm the BA covers both Redwood managed storage and any logs kept in Dedicated.
[07:05] Alex Monroe: We'll confirm and call out which components are covered and provide the BA language. If you require BA-only for Private on-prem we can add that to the enterprise agreement.
[07:16] [07:16] Miguel Torres: Ok, on technical details — Priya, can you outline what we'd need to set up a Dedicated pool in EU only and integrate our KMS?
[07:22] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Steps: 1) Provision Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1; 2) Configure network access with VPC peering or private link; 3) Set up customer-managed KMS key and provide ARN/credentials for envelope encryption; 4) Configure logging toggles and retention policies; 5) Validate RBAC/SSO via SAML integration; 6) Run benchmark with sample workload. I'll share a runbook that walks through each step.
[07:47] Sam Patel: For SSO, we use Okta. We need SCIM for user provisioning and SAML for SSO.
[07:53] Priya Kapoor: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll include an Okta quickstart.
[07:59] Karen Liu: Any known limitations with PCI scoped data? Some of our merchants process payments and we want to know if Redwood can be in-scope without adding risk.
[08:08] Alex Monroe: PCI is tricky because tokenized card data should never be sent to LLMs. We recommend client-side tokenization and never send raw PANs. For audit purposes, we can show controls that prevent transmission of cardholder data and offer redaction patterns in middleware.
[08:22] Miguel Torres: Good. Let's talk timeline — ideally we want a pilot in a couple of weeks to show stakeholders. Is that feasible?
[08:29] Alex Monroe: Yes, for a focused pilot using Dedicated we can target pilot start in two to three weeks assuming DPA and BA are signed and we have sample data. For Private on-prem it'll be longer.
[08:39] Sam Patel: What about logging restriction enforcement — can you prevent developers from enabling full logging accidentally?
[08:44] Priya Kapoor: Yes, RBAC + policy enforcement at the route level. We can lock down logging flags to admins and provide templates with logging disabled for sensitive routes.
[08:55] Karen Liu: We'll need evidence of encryption in transit and at rest and proof that keys are in our control for Private.
[09:01] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide TLS details, cipher suites, and KMS integration docs. For Private, keys remain in customer KMS so you control root access.
[09:11] Alex Monroe: Any other blockers we should know about?
[09:14] Miguel Torres: One more: regulatory audits sometimes require data residency proofs. Can you produce attestation that data processed for EU customers never left EU hosts?
[09:24] Priya Kapoor: For Dedicated pinned to EU we can provide logs and attestations proving processing occurred in-region. For Hosted it's more complicated but we can provide flow diagrams and contractual commitments for data locality if needed.
[09:39] [09:39] Sam Patel: On the pilot benchmarks — we'll want to test throughput for concurrent sessions and also cold-start KV cache behavior. Does Redwood support warm-up hooks?
[09:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have APIs for pre-warming KV cache and continuous batching settings. We'll include those in the runbook and help craft a benchmark harness.
[09:58] Karen Liu: From a procurement perspective, who do we sign with? Is there a US entity and EU entity?
[10:05] Alex Monroe: We have a US entity for North America contracts; for EU customers we can contract with our EU subsidiary or use cross-border DPA specifics. We'll get legal involved to advise the right entity.
[10:19] Miguel Torres: Ok, sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[10:22] Alex Monroe: Recap: Alex sends SOC2, HIPAA docs, DPA template, subprocessors list. Priya schedules technical deep-dive and shares runbook and benchmark scripts. Sam will share sample workload and PII/PHI list. Karen will share retention and redaction requirements and legal contacts. Target pilot start week of 2026-03-30. Does that capture it?
[10:43] Karen Liu: Yes.
[10:45] Sam Patel: Yes.
[10:46] Alex Monroe: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and doc pack.
[10:52] Miguel Torres: Thanks.
[10:53] [00:10:53] Speaker 1: (background noise)
[00:11:00] Alex Monroe: Alright, we'll leave it there.
[00:11:03] Karen Liu: Thanks, bye.
